observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of an active fire: several thin wooden sticks/branches lie in a roughly fixed pile, with bright orange-yellow flames licking over and around them against a dark background. A stick protrudes at the left edge, a horizontal stick with a prominent knot sits in the center, and a diagonal forked stick occupies the upper right. The scene is already burning at the first frame and is still burning at the last.
visible_changes: The flames continuously deform, rise, and change shape throughout the segment; no two frames show the same flame outline.
In the early frames (1-14) the dominant flame is a tall plume on the left, while the central and right sticks are mostly exposed.
From about frames 15-27 the flame volume spreads rightward and upward, brightening the center and partially covering the sticks.
Around frames 28-33 a large, very bright flame mass engulfs the central and right sticks, heavily occluding them; by frames 34-41 this mass thins and the sticks re-emerge more clearly.
The sticks' positions relative to the frame edges stay essentially constant across all frames; their apparent appearing/disappearing is due to flame occlusion, not stick movement.
Overall luminance and flame height fluctuate from frame to frame without a single directional trend.
The wood shows no obvious structural collapse or rapid consumption within this short excerpt; the stick arrangement persists.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the fire or how long it had been burning before frame 1.
Whether the sticks eventually burn away or the fire dies out after frame 41.
The wider setting around the fire (only dark background is visible).
uncertain_details: Whether there is slight handheld camera drift or jitter; the sticks' stable edge positions suggest little or no deliberate pan/zoom, but minor motion cannot be ruled out.
The exact material/identity of the sticks (only that they are thin woody pieces).
Distinguishing true flame expansion from changes in brightness/exposure is approximate.
